column1: # ST-<state><armed><calibrated><faults>, nine bytes on the air with its separators, carried on
# every rich packet it fits. It is how the console knows the vehicle's mission state, whether
# it is armed and calibrated, and how many faults are active, now that the five diagnostic tags
# are off the air to make room for GPS and sound inside the organizers' 200-byte limit.
#   state       I INIT, T SELF_TEST, R READY, F FLIGHT, L LANDED, V RECOVERY, X FAULT
#   faults      active fault count, 0 to 9 -- 9 means nine or more
# Both ground parsers expand it into the MODE, ARM, CAL and FAULTS tags the console and the
# CSV already read, and the firmware encodes it. All three read this file:
# Format: <id> TAB <value after "ST-"> TAB <MODE> TAB <ARM> TAB <CAL> TAB <FAULTS>
# A row whose MODE is "-" is not a status field: the firmware never produces it, and a parser
# must leave all four tags absent rather than guess.
